sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Application Gateway health monitoring overview (health probes)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-18. The default probe sends an HTTP GET to <protocol>://127.0.0.1:<port>/ every 30 seconds with an unhealthy threshold of 3; 'By default, an HTTP(S) response with status code between 200 and 399 is considered healthy'; custom probes set the host, path, interval, timeout and threshold and can match status codes or body text; unhealthy servers stop receiving traffic; a misconfigured probe path is linked to 502 Bad Gateway errors. That a backend returning 401 on / is marked unhealthy follows from the 200-399 default, stated as the author's.

brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Brookfield College. The student portal runs on three VMs behind Application Gateway agw-portal (v2) with the default health probe. Last night's release put the whole site behind sign-in: / now returns 401 unless a user is signed in, and a new /healthz page returns 200. Since 07:55 every request through the gateway gets 502 Bad Gateway. Course enrollment opens at 09:00.
handover: The VMs answer normally when reached directly from the jump box.
The release notes mention /healthz 'for the load balancer'; nobody changed the gateway.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the gateway's listener, its health probe, the backend pool of three VMs and the pages they serve.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

probe.label: Create a custom probe for /healthz (200-399) and attach it to the portal's HTTP settings
probe.available: not busy and (not fixed and not harmed)
probe.why: Already done, or the system is down.

effects.output:
neteng@cloudshell:~$ az network application-gateway probe create -g rg-portal --gateway-name agw-portal -n probe-healthz --protocol Https --path /healthz --host-name-from-http-settings true --interval 30 --threshold 3 --match-status-codes 200-399

writeup.question: For the record: why the gateway returned 502, what you changed, and how it stays fixed.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The release put / behind sign-in; the default probe requests / and accepts 200-399, got 401 from all three VMs, marked them unhealthy, and the gateway had nowhere to send requests.

parts.label: Changed
parts.modelAnswer: A custom probe for /healthz with 200-399, attached to the HTTP settings; the backends turned healthy. Turning off sign-in would have exposed student records; scaling the gateway changes nothing.

parts.label: Stays fixed
parts.modelAnswer: The probe is in the Bicep template and an alert fires when healthy hosts drop below two.

scoring.modelReasoning: A 502 for everyone with healthy VMs points at the probe. Backend health shows 401 from every server: the default probe requests /, which now needs sign-in, and only 200-399 count as healthy. Create a custom probe for /healthz with 200-399, attach it to the HTTP settings, and check health and the portal. Turning off sign-in exposes records; scaling the gateway probes the same path.
